binding.applicability_statement: Results attest only to this witness code build and this exact input file on the sandboxed CPython that executes it; they do not attest to the seed draft's claims in general, to other implementations or releases, or to inputs outside this fixture set. The sandbox certifies process isolation only, never oracle truth.

units_and_domain.accepted_input_domain: I-JSON (RFC 7493) per RFC 8785 section 3.1: no duplicate object names; strings expressible as Unicode (lone surrogates error per section 3.2.2.2 Note); numbers expressible as IEEE 754 binary64 (NaN and Infinity error per section 3.2.2.3 Note)
units_and_domain.duplicate_name_policy: reject with error; no first-wins/last-wins merge defined by the source
units_and_domain.number_units: IEEE 754 binary64 doubles; serialization per ECMA-262 7.1.12.1 including Note 2, sampled by RFC 8785 Appendix B Table 1
units_and_domain.string_units: Unicode code points for serialization; UTF-16 code units (unsigned, non-locale) for property-name sorting

citations: RFC 8785 section 3.2.3: UTF-16 code-unit order puts U+1F600 (units D83D DE00) before U+FB33; code-point or UTF-8-byte order reverses the pair
RFC 8785 section 3.2.3: raw unescaped form (newline treated as U+000A), ascending example "" < "a" < "aa" < "ab"; discriminates sorting on escaped text where "1" would precede "\r"
RFC 8785 section 3.1 via RFC 7493: objects MUST NOT exhibit duplicate property names; "A" and "\u0041" denote the same name after escape resolution
RFC 8785 section 3.1 via RFC 7493: duplicate property names are out of domain; no merge policy is defined
RFC 8785 section 3.1 Note and section 3.2.2.2: strings preserved as is; no normalization applied
RFC 8785 section 3.1 Note: JCS does not take Unicode normalization into consideration; all components MUST preserve string data as is. Pair with c-f09: outputs must differ byte-wise
RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.2 Note: lone surrogates (e.g. U+DEAD) MUST cause termination with an appropriate error
RFC 8785 sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.2.3: equal doubles share one output token regardless of input spelling
RFC 8785 Appendix B Table 1 rows 1-2: zero and minus zero both serialize as 0
RFC 8785 Appendix B Table 1 rows 17-19 and section 3.2.2 sample: 1e+21 fixed/exponent boundary, 1e-6 fixed floor, 1e-27 exponent form, spelled-out forms collapse to ES6 tokens
RFC 8785 Appendix B Table 1 row 26 and note 4: exactly 1424953923781206.25 truncates/rounds per ECMA-262 Note 2 to 1424953923781206.2 (closest even choice)
RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.3 Note: Infinity is not permitted and MUST cause an error; overflow literals 1e309/-1e309 reach binary64 as Infinity
RFC 8785 Appendix D sample: giantNumber 1.4e+9999 overflows binary64 to Infinity, which MUST error per section 3.2.2.3 Note

RFC 8785 sections 3.1 (numbers MUST be expressible as IEEE 754 double) and 3.2.2 (numbers are subject to rounding): 9007199254740993 parses to the nearest double 9007199254740992; strict domain acceptance of such literals is recorded as an open domain question, not settled here
RFC 8785 Appendix B Table 1 quoted verbatim (26 rows); rows for NaN and Infinity show no JSON representation per note 3

wrong_implementations.description: plausible wrong implementation: sorts property names by Unicode code point (equivalently UTF-8/UTF-32 byte order) instead of UTF-16 code units
plausible wrong implementation: sorts property names by their JSON-escaped text instead of raw unescaped form
plausible wrong implementation: serializes numbers with Python repr instead of ECMA-262 7.1.12.1 (wrong zero and exponent-window forms, no NaN/Infinity prohibition)
plausible wrong implementation: applies NFC normalization to strings and names instead of preserving them as is
plausible wrong implementation: default parser behavior that silently merges duplicate names last-wins instead of rejecting
plausible wrong implementation: replaces lone surrogates with U+FFFD and continues instead of terminating with an error
plausible wrong implementation: emits separators with spaces, violating the no-whitespace rule
